title: Durable reviewer calibration record and its installing command
description:
PREREQUISITE of task-4dd4424c1c264f4490bcb7cad01e7585 (Production verifier authority provider), which is itself GAP E of task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a (Foundation self-host canary). Sibling of task-92031b0a64f74b08b4278b94db67dee6; the two are independent and can run in parallel.

MEASURED GAP at committed HEAD a42ae2f (git grep against HEAD, not the working tree):

  git grep -n "ReviewerCalibration" HEAD -- apps/ packages/ | grep -v '\.test\.'

ReviewerCalibration is declared at packages/review/src/review-contract.ts:128 as
  { corpusRevision: string; sentinelPassed: boolean; staleness: ReviewCalibrationStaleness }
with the doc comment "Design 15.3 currency and sentinel gate. Both are caller-supplied durable facts."

It is CONSUMED at packages/review/src/reviewer-eligibility.ts:116 and :135 and is a required field of VerifierAuthorityFacts (apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:16) and of the stored VerifierReceiptV1 (:42). But the ONLY thing on disk that ever produces one is the test fixture apps/daemon/src/review/review-test-fixtures.ts:249. There is no command, no event, and no durable record. apps/daemon/src/review/review-acceptance.ts:116 only reads one back OUT of an already-recorded receipt, so it cannot be the source.

The contract calls the facts "caller-supplied DURABLE facts" -- caller-supplied is the intended authority model, but DURABLE is the half that is missing: today a caller could only supply them in-process, per call, unattested.

WHY IT BLOCKS. task-4dd4424c must produce VerifierAuthorityFacts.calibration from a durable record. With no writer, the only ways to satisfy it are to default the field, mint it in the wrapper, or read it from a node spec file that any agent in the shared tree can write -- all forbidden by global rail Clause 2 and epic rail 4, and all explicitly refused by the shipped comment at apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts:239.

Objective: give reviewer calibration a durable home written by a real authenticated command, and a focused reader that returns it or fails closed.

Deliverable: the durable record plus its reader plus focused tests. RESOLVE THE MECHANISM AT PLANNING TIME by measurement, and record the decision: the leading candidate is the EXISTING policy.install slice mechanism (apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-services.ts:42-61 folds {slices:{[sliceRef]:slice}} behind a PolicyInstalled event, with the payload allow-list ["slice"] at daemon-command-registry.ts:113), which would require no new command kind and no runtime-vocabulary change. Only introduce a dedicated command kind if measurement shows the slice mechanism genuinely cannot carry it -- and note that the runtime command vocabulary is frozen with a full-coverage ratchet, so adding a kind is a far larger change than it looks.

NOT in scope: changing the ReviewerCalibration shape, reviewer-eligibility's rules, VerifierAuthorityFacts, the receipt ledger, or anything under tests/e2e/foundation.
definitionOfDone: Planning notes record the chosen durable mechanism with the measurement behind it, and state explicitly whether a new runtime command kind was required and why; reusing policy.install's slice mechanism is preferred and a new kind must be justified against the frozen-vocabulary ratchet.

A real authenticated command durably records a ReviewerCalibration for a project; a test drives that command through the production registry and asserts the stored record's corpusRevision, sentinelPassed and staleness are byte-identical to what was installed.

A focused reader returns the stored calibration; with no record installed it returns an exact stable not-found code and layer and NO calibration -- a test pins both literals and asserts the raw store event count is unchanged on the read path.

A malformed or partially-specified calibration (missing sentinelPassed, an unknown staleness value, a non-string corpusRevision) is refused at the ingress layer with its exact code, and nothing is committed; the generated hostile-case count is asserted nonzero.
A mutation drill on the durable read makes a NAMED test go red for its calibration-value assertion (not for a crash), and production bytes are restored exactly.

The completion note names task-4dd4424c1c264f4490bcb7cad01e7585 as the production consumer; pnpm typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exit 0 with a nonzero printed Test Files count line, and owned production files are each <=250 physical lines.
taskRails: Fail closed with stable reason codes; an absent calibration is a refusal, never a default, and never an optimistic pass of the sentinel gate.
Prefer the existing durable slice mechanism over minting a runtime command kind; the command vocabulary is frozen with a full-coverage ratchet and widening it is a separate, larger decision.
Do not change the ReviewerCalibration shape or reviewer-eligibility's rules; this task supplies the missing durable writer and reader only.
Use TDD. Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400. Stage and commit only explicit owned paths by pathspec; no git add -A, no worktree, no push, no merge.

implementationPlan.description: Confirm the mechanism decision on committed HEAD before writing code. Read-only. The architect's decision, recorded in this plan's planningNotes as DoD 1 requires, is REUSE `policy.install` -- NO new runtime command kind. Re-verify the four facts it rests on with `git grep`/`git show`: (1) `installPolicy` (apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-services.ts:42-61) takes `payloadObject(request.payload, "slice")`, requires `payloadRef(slice, "sliceRef")`, folds `{slices: {...current, [sliceRef]: slice}}` and commits a `PolicyInstalled` event -- so a slice is an arbitrary JsonObject addressed by a caller-chosen ref, which carries `{corpusRevision, sentinelPassed, staleness}` without any shape change; (2) the read shape is `installedSlices(stateOf(ledger, aggregateId))` (:28-35) over the same aggregate `aggregateIdFor(request, null)` gives; (3) `policy.install` is already registered with capability ADMIN and payload allow-list `["slice"]` (apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts:53, :113), so the authenticated write path already exists and this task adds a READER, not a writer; (4) the runtime command vocabulary is frozen with a full-coverage ratchet, which is why adding a kind would be a far larger change than it looks. If any of the four is false on current bytes, STOP and re-decide in the step note before continuing -- do not silently fall back to minting a kind.
implementationPlan.note:
Mechanism decision CONFIRMED on committed HEAD 29e1b45 (HEAD moved from the plan's a42ae2f; all four facts still hold). REUSE policy.install; NO new runtime command kind.

(1) installPolicy (bootstrap-policy-services.ts:42-61) takes payloadObject(request.payload,"slice"), requires payloadRef(slice,"sliceRef"), folds {slices:{...current,[sliceRef]:slice}} and commits PolicyInstalled — an arbitrary JsonObject under a caller-chosen ref. VERIFIED verbatim.
(2) read shape installedSlices(stateOf(ledger, aggregateId)) (:28-35); aggregateIdFor(request,null) returns `${projectId}-policy` for policy.install/policy.validate (bootstrap-sequence.ts:47-52). VERIFIED.
(3) policy.install registered capability ADMIN (daemon-command-registry.ts:53) with payload allow-list ["slice"] (:113). VERIFIED — the authenticated durable WRITE path already exists; this task ships the READER.
(4) runtime command vocabulary frozen with a full-coverage ratchet (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts + runtime-contract.test.ts, plus control-room generated-coverage.test.ts and mcp stdio-schemas.test.ts). Not adding a kind, so untouched.

FOUR NEW FACTS the plan did not carry, all load-bearing:

(a) COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["policy.install"] === Object.freeze([]) (bootstrap-sequence.ts:26). A calibration slice installs on a FRESH store with no bootstrap setup — no driveThrough needed, expectedVersion 0 then 1 on the `${projectId}-policy` aggregate.

(b) NULL-PROTOTYPE HAZARD. stateOf() returns decodeResult(resultBytes) = decodeBoundedJsonBytes, and that parser builds objects with Object.create(null) (packages/contracts/src/bounded-json-parser.ts:87; asserted at bounded-json-hostile.test.ts:209). So the slice the reader reads back is a null-prototype object. The reader must NOT use a prototype-identity guard. Note verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:isObject REQUIRES getPrototypeOf===null for exactly this reason — copying its guard shape blindly would be wrong here in the opposite direction is not the risk; the risk is copying a plain `instanceof Object`/inherited-key assumption. Use typeof==="object" && !==null && !Array.isArray plus Object.hasOwn.

(c) SECURITY-LANE RATCHET, invisible to this task's gate. tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts:243 scans production sources with DECLARATION_PATTERN = /^export const ([A-Z_]+(?:LAYERS|LAYER|BOUNDARIES))\s*(?::[^=]+)?=/u against a hand-written 89-entry table. Exporting any `*_LAYER`/`*_LAYERS`/`*_BOUNDARIES` constant reddens `pnpm test:security`, which neither `pnpm typecheck` nor `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` runs. DECISION: this task exports NO layer constant. The refusal carries a `layer` FIELD whose value reuses the existing ServiceRefusedBy vocabulary from bootstrap-ledger.ts; exported constants are REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_SLICE_REF and REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_REFUSAL_CODES, neither matching the pattern.

(d) REVIEW VOCABULARY RATCHET. review-refusal-vocabulary.test.ts asserts BOTH directions over REVIEW_INGRESS_REFUSAL_CODES + REVIEW_PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES (review-contracts.ts:56,76) — every declared code must actually be emitted by runReviewCommand. Adding this reader's codes there would create a dead entry and redden it. DECISION: the reader declares its own frozen vocabulary local to reviewer-calibration-record.ts. It is a durable READER, not a review command surface, so it does not belong in either list.

Chosen refusal vocabulary (distinct per cause, no collision with PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES nor with @moe/review's REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_STALE/UNPROVEN): REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_NOT_INSTALLED (no slice under the ref) and REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_UNREADABLE (slice present, contents malformed). Both at layer DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, matching the BOOTSTRAP_POLICY_UNKNOWN and REVIEW_LINEAGE_UNREADABLE precedents. The other answering layer is DAEMON_INGRESS (installPolicy's generic BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID on a missing sliceRef) — that is the write/read division step-4 must pin.

Supporting facts: @moe/review dependency edge holds (apps/daemon/package.json dependencies + pnpm-lock apps/daemon importer line ~111); REVIEW_CALIBRATION_STALENESS and ReviewerCalibration both exported from the @moe/review root (index.ts:22,66). bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts `send` drives the PRODUCTION pipeline (runBootstrapCommand) and has no prerequisite coupling for policy.install. store.readEventsAfter(0n,N).items is the raw event count DoD 3 needs. Read-only step; no files modified.

implementationPlan.description: RED, in a new apps/daemon/src/review/reviewer-calibration-record.test.ts against a REAL SqliteEventStore. Drive the REAL `policy.install` command through the production registry -- not a hand-written event, or the test proves a shape production would never write. Failing tests: (1) after installing a calibration slice under the well-known sliceRef, `readReviewerCalibration(store, projectId)` returns exactly `{corpusRevision, sentinelPassed, staleness}` byte-identical to what was installed -- assert each field's value, never `toBeTruthy`; (2) with NO slice installed it returns an exact stable not-found code and layer and NO calibration -- assert both literals, and assert the store's raw event count is unchanged by the read; (3) a slice installed under the right ref but malformed -- missing `sentinelPassed`, a `staleness` outside the frozen `REVIEW_CALIBRATION_STALENESS` set `["CURRENT","STALE","UNKNOWN"]`, a non-string or absent `corpusRevision`, a non-boolean `sentinelPassed` -- refuses with a DISTINCT stable code from case (2), because "nothing installed" and "installed but unreadable" are different facts and collapsing them makes a later guard change invisible; (4) a LATER `policy.install` under the same ref supersedes the earlier one and the reader returns the newer value, since installPolicy's fold is last-write-wins per ref. Assert the generated malformed-case count is nonzero before asserting the cases.
implementationPlan.note:
RED confirmed for the right reason. Command run in the FOREGROUND from apps/daemon:
  npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/review/reviewer-calibration-record.test.ts
Output: "Error: Cannot find module './reviewer-calibration-record.js' imported from .../reviewer-calibration-record.test.ts" -> "Test Files 1 failed (1)". Fails because the module is missing, not because of a typo or a wrong import path (the other two imports, ../daemon-command-registry.js and ../http/http-contract.js, resolved).

WHAT DRIVES THE WRITE. Not the bootstrap-test-fixtures `send` helper and not a hand-written event: the test builds createDaemonCommandPorts({clock, operatorPrincipalId, projectId, store}) over an ephemeral SqliteEventStore, pulls registry.get("policy.install") -- the exact CommandRegistry object the HTTP seam reads -- and commits through ports.decisions.decide(key, digest, () => entry.handler({envelope, principal})). That is the production registry AND production's own refusal translation: entry.handler throws an internal DomainRefusal and the decision port converts it to {outcome:"REFUSED", refusal:{code, layer}}. Catching the throw myself would have graded a crash as a refusal; going through the port grades what production actually reports. The envelope is a real RuntimeCommandEnvelope at RUNTIME_COMMAND_ENVELOPE_VERSION and the principal carries capability project.admin, matching the registry's ADMIN requirement measured in step 1.

DURABLE SHAPE CHOSEN: the slice is FLAT -- {sliceRef, corpusRevision, sentinelPassed, staleness}. sliceRef is the address installPolicy requires; the other three are the ReviewerCalibration verbatim, no shape change (task rail 3). Flat plus an exact-key requirement gives the reader a strong malformed guard: an extra field is unreadable rather than silently ignored, which is the `exact()` convention verifier-receipt-contracts.ts already uses.

WELL-KNOWN REF IS DELIBERATELY HUMAN-READABLE, not hex64, and that is the answer to step 4's open question about validatePolicy visibility. Measured: packages/core/src/policy/policy-validation.ts:218 is `if (!validHex64(input["policyRevisionRef"])) return undefined;`. So a policy.validate naming the calibration ref clears installPolicy's Object.hasOwn check but can NEVER be accepted -- evaluatePolicy refuses it at layer CORE_REDUCER because the ref is not 64 hex. The calibration slice is therefore unnameable by any ACCEPTED policy evaluation. bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:118-122 records the same asymmetry from the other direction. Step 4 will pin this with a test rather than leave it as prose.

TESTS WRITTEN (13 cases across 2 describes), all asserting values, never truthiness:
1. reads back byte-identically -- installs {corpus-abc, false, STALE} (deliberately NOT the all-default-looking {non-empty, true, CURRENT}, so a hard-coded return cannot accidentally match) and asserts each of the three fields plus Object.keys(...).sort() === ["corpusRevision","sentinelPassed","staleness"], which pins that sliceRef is stripped.
2. absent record -- asserts code REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_NOT_INSTALLED, layer DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, `"calibration" in read === false`, and raw store event count via store.readEventsAfter(0n,1_000).items.length unchanged across the read.
3. NEW CASE not in the plan, added because the plan's step-6 self-review asks it: a slice installed under a DIFFERENT ref must not be mistaken for the calibration one. Without it, a reader that returned "the first slice" or "any slice" would pass every other case.
4. supersession -- old {corpus-old,false,UNKNOWN} at expectedVersion 0 then new {corpus-new,true,CURRENT} at expectedVersion 1 under the same ref; reader must return the newer, per installPolicy's last-write-wins fold.
5. hostile sweep of 9 generated malformed-contents cases: absent/non-boolean sentinelPassed, absent/non-string/empty corpusRevision, absent/out-of-set/lower-case staleness, and an unlisted extra field. Each asserts code UNREADABLE, `not.toBe(NOT_INSTALLED)` so the two facts stay distinct, layer DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, and no calibration key.
6. sweep-nonzero guard: asserts MALFORMED_SLICES.length > 0 AND toHaveLength(9) AND that REVIEW_CALIBRATION_STALENESS imported from the bare @moe/review specifier equals ["CURRENT","STALE","UNKNOWN"] AND that at least one generated case actually carries a staleness outside that set -- so the sweep cannot go vacuous in either direction.

ANTI-VACUITY GUARD: installAccepted() throws if any install is refused. Every malformed case must be ACCEPTED by installPolicy (which requires only a sliceRef), which is what proves the refusal under test belongs to this task's reader and not to the pre-existing generic BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID ingress guard. A fixture that silently got refused at ingress would otherwise leave nine green cases testing a guard they never reach.

Store handles are pushed to an array and closed in afterEach -- a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN. Create apps/daemon/src/review/reviewer-calibration-record.ts plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./reviewer-calibration-record.ts";` -- without it the module is invisible to the .js import graph). Export the well-known sliceRef as a frozen named constant so tests and the eventual consumer assert a symbol rather than a bare string, and export `readReviewerCalibration(store, projectId)` returning a frozen `ReviewerCalibration` or a refusal carrying a stable code and layer. Validate `staleness` against the PUBLIC `REVIEW_CALIBRATION_STALENESS` imported from the bare `@moe/review` specifier -- do not restate the three members locally, or the check silently detaches the day the set changes. THE CRITICAL REFUSAL RULE: when no slice is installed, REFUSE. Do NOT return `{corpusRevision: "", sentinelPassed: false, staleness: "UNKNOWN"}`. That value is a perfectly legal ReviewerCalibration and `calibrationCodes` (packages/review/src/reviewer-eligibility.ts:116-126) would map it to `REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_UNPROVEN`, which LOOKS fail-closed but is fabrication: it asserts a calibration exists and is unproven, when the truth is that none exists at all. The contract's own comment is explicit -- "UNKNOWN is unproven, never 'probably fine'" -- and epic rail 4 requires missing evidence to stay UNKNOWN without gaining authority, not to be synthesised into a legal record. Perform no writes. Keep the file <=250 physical lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/review/reviewer-calibration-record.test.ts` from apps/daemon, FOREGROUND: "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 14 passed (14)". A nonzero executed-test count line, so the run is evidence rather than a vacuous exit 0.

SHIPPED, three files, all new:
- apps/daemon/src/review/reviewer-calibration-record.ts, 152 physical lines (cap 250).
- apps/daemon/src/review/reviewer-calibration-record.js, 1 line: `export * from "./reviewer-calibration-record.ts";` -- without it the module is invisible to the .js import graph.
- (test from step 2, 241 lines.)

SURFACE. REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_SLICE_REF = "moe-reviewer-calibration/1"; REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_REFUSAL_CODES = frozen ["REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_NOT_INSTALLED","REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_UNREADABLE"]; type ReviewerCalibrationRefusalCode; type ReviewerCalibrationRead (discriminated union); readReviewerCalibration(store, projectId). NO runtime command kind added. NO writer added -- policy.install already is the authenticated writer.

DECISIONS WORTH GRADING:

1. THE REFUSAL RULE, implemented as a union rather than an optional field. The refusal branch has no `calibration` key at all, so a synthesised {corpusRevision:"", sentinelPassed:false, staleness:"UNKNOWN"} is not merely discouraged, it is unrepresentable on that branch. That value is legal and calibrationCodes maps it to REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_UNPROVEN, so it would have looked fail-closed while fabricating a durable fact. The comment at refuse() states this so a later editor cannot "simplify" it back.

2. AGGREGATE ID ASKED OF PRODUCTION, NOT RESTATED. policyAggregateId() calls aggregateIdFor({kind:"policy.install", projectId} as unknown as BootstrapRequest, null) rather than hard-coding `${projectId}-policy`. aggregateIdFor reads only those two properties (verified at bootstrap-sequence.ts:47-56). A literal would have detached silently the day the policy case moves; this follows it.

3. STALENESS VALIDATED AGAINST THE IMPORTED PUBLIC SET. isStaleness() tests membership of REVIEW_CALIBRATION_STALENESS imported from the bare @moe/review specifier -- no local restatement of ["CURRENT","STALE","UNKNOWN"] anywhere in the production file. Note verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:parseCalibration DOES restate them inline; this module deliberately does not, per the plan.

4. NULL-PROTOTYPE SAFE. asObject() uses typeof/Array.isArray/null tests only, and membership goes through Object.hasOwn -- the ledger's state comes back through decodeBoundedJsonBytes, which builds objects with Object.create(null). An `instanceof`, a prototype-identity check, or a plain `in` would have been wrong here.

5. EXACT-KEY SLICE. A calibration slice must carry exactly {corpusRevision, sentinelPassed, sliceRef, staleness}. An extra field is UNREADABLE rather than ignored, so nothing can be smuggled past a consumer that reads it later. corpusRevision must be a non-empty string: an empty one is what reviewer-eligibility already treats as never-proven, so an empty durable record is not a record.

6. NO LAYER CONSTANT EXPORTED. DURABLE_READ_LAYER is module-private and typed `ServiceRefusedBy`, so it cannot drift out of the daemon's shared vocabulary without a compile error, while not matching tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts's /^export const ([A-Z_]+(?:LAYERS|LAYER|BOUNDARIES))/ scan. Neither exported constant matches that pattern. pnpm test:security therefore stays untouched by this task -- a gate that neither pnpm typecheck nor the filtered daemon test run would have caught.

7. READS ONLY. readDurableLedger(store, projectId) is called and returns; no store handle is retained past the call, no commit path exists in the module.

Zero errors name any reviewer-calibration-record file; measured explicitly by filtering the tsc output for that name and getting 0.

The foreign set MOVED DURING THIS STEP, which is worth recording: the first run also carried 5 errors in apps/daemon/src/review/review-services.test.ts (TS2304 BOUND_ITEMS/itemsOf/itemKey) and those CLEARED on the immediately following run with no action from me -- the sibling task-92031b0a landed apps/daemon/src/review/review-round-items.ts mid-run. So this package's baseline is moving under peer writes; step 7 re-measures rather than trusting this reading. Owned-path intersection with the failing set is EMPTY in both readings.

implementationPlan.description: Cover the ingress refusals that belong to the WRITE path, and be honest about which layer owns them. `policy.install`'s payload allow-list is `["slice"]` and `installPolicy` refuses `BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID` at layer `DAEMON_INGRESS` when the slice or its `sliceRef` is missing -- that guard is generic and already exists, so it is NOT this task's to reimplement. What this task must decide and test is the boundary: a slice installed under the calibration ref whose CONTENTS are malformed passes `installPolicy` (it only requires a sliceRef) and is caught by this task's READER. Write tests that pin exactly that division -- assert which layer refused in each case, since two layers can answer here and a test asserting only "refused" is one guard away from vacuous. Also record the review item this raises: a calibration slice becomes visible to `validatePolicy` (bootstrap-policy-services.ts:64-80) as an installed ref, so its `BOOTSTRAP_POLICY_UNKNOWN` check would pass for the calibration ref. Decide whether that is acceptable (it likely is -- `evaluatePolicy` judges the caller's input, not the slice) and state the decision rather than leaving it unexamined.
implementationPlan.note:
Layer division pinned by test, and the validatePolicy question DECIDED by measurement rather than left as prose. `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/review/reviewer-calibration-record.test.ts` from apps/daemon, FOREGROUND: "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 21 passed (21)" (was 14; +7 this step). No production file touched -- this step is test-only, which is correct because the ingress guard it exercises already exists and is not this task's to reimplement.

THE DIVISION, three cases, each asserting WHICH layer answered:

1. `registers policy.install under ADMIN with the exact allow-list [slice]` -- asserts the production registry entry's requiredCapability === "project.admin" and payloadKeys === ["slice"]. This pins what the HTTP seam enforces without re-testing the seam: daemon-command-registry.test.ts already drives the allow-list refusal (stage PAYLOAD_SHAPE, INPUT_INVALID, 400) for all 23 kinds including policy.install, so duplicating it here would add a second owner for one rule.

2. `refuses ... at DAEMON_INGRESS, which is not this task's guard` -- three swept cases (a slice with no sliceRef; a sliceRef that is the empty string; a slice that is a string rather than an object). Each asserts code BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID AND layer DAEMON_INGRESS AND that the raw store event count is 0, so the generic guard is shown to commit nothing.

3. `accepts malformed CONTENTS at ingress and leaves the refusal to the reader` -- THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. It asserts the POSITIVE half: a slice with staleness "PROBABLY_FINE" but a valid sliceRef is DECIDED by installPolicy and durably commits (rawEventCount 1), and only then does readReviewerCalibration refuse it with REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_UNREADABLE at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE. Without this, the nine-case malformed sweep from step 2 could have been passing because installPolicy refused first, and the reader would never have been exercised at all -- exactly the "refusal test answered by an earlier guard" failure. The sweep's installAccepted() helper throws on a refused setup, but a helper's throw is not an assertion a reader can grade; this is the named case that states it.

THE validatePolicy DECISION, and it is NOT the one the plan guessed. The plan expected "acceptable because evaluatePolicy judges the caller's input, not the slice". That is true but incomplete, and the incomplete version would have left a real hazard unexamined. MEASURED: validatePolicy checks Object.hasOwn(installed, policyRef) BEFORE calling evaluatePolicy, so a calibration slice genuinely DOES clear the daemon's BOOTSTRAP_POLICY_UNKNOWN presence gate. The safety does not come from the daemon at all -- it comes from packages/core/src/policy/policy-validation.ts:218, `if (!validHex64(input["policyRevisionRef"])) return undefined;`. That is why REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_SLICE_REF is deliberately "moe-reviewer-calibration/1" and NOT 64 hex: a hex64 calibration ref would have been nameable as a policy revision and would have had to be defended somewhere else. bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:118-122 records the same asymmetry from the opposite direction ("a slice installed under a human-readable ref could never be named by a valid evaluation input").

Tested as a PAIR, because either half alone proves nothing:
- foreign ref installed, validate names the calibration ref -> BOOTSTRAP_POLICY_UNKNOWN at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE. This is the negative control; it establishes that the presence gate is what answers when the ref is genuinely absent.
- calibration ref installed, same input -> refusal at CORE_REDUCER with code INPUT_INVALID. Reaching a DIFFERENT layer is the proof it got past the presence gate; INPUT_INVALID is the proof the core stopped it. The case also re-reads the record afterwards and asserts corpusRevision is intact, so a validate attempt cannot damage the record.
The negative control is not decoration: without it, CORE_REDUCER alone would be consistent with the presence gate having been skipped for some other reason.

I pinned INPUT_INVALID concretely rather than only asserting "not BOOTSTRAP_POLICY_UNKNOWN". Epic rail 6 wants the specific stable code, and INPUT_INVALID is a public @moe/contracts RuntimeErrorCode returned at policy-evaluation.ts:169, not an internal detail.

Test helper refactor this step required: envelopeFor now takes the kind, and openProject exposes dispatch(kind, payload, commandId, expectedVersion) plus entryFor(kind) alongside install(). Every path still goes through ports.decisions.decide over the real registry entry -- nothing was loosened to make these cases fit. Test file now 365 lines; the 250-line cap is per PRODUCTION file and reviewer-calibration-record.ts is unchanged at 152.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills, three, one per distinct claim, because a green suite cannot tell a real durable read from a default. Drill 1 (the durable read is load-bearing): make `readReviewerCalibration` return a hard-coded literal instead of the stored slice; the step-2 case (1) test must go RED on a field-value comparison, not on a crash. Drill 2 (absent must refuse, not synthesise): make the not-found branch return `{corpusRevision: "", sentinelPassed: false, staleness: "UNKNOWN"}`; the step-2 case (2) test must go RED. This is the load-bearing drill -- that value is legal, so only a test asserting the REFUSAL code can catch it, and if it stays green the test is asserting the wrong thing. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: THE MECHANISM DECISION REQUIRED BY DoD 1: REUSE `policy.install`; do NOT mint a runtime command kind. Measurement behind it, all at committed HEAD a42ae2f: `installPolicy` (apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-services.ts:42-61) accepts an arbitrary JsonObject `slice` addressed by a caller-chosen `sliceRef`, folds `{slices: {...current, [sliceRef]: slice}}` and commits a `PolicyInstalled` event; the read shape is `installedSlices(stateOf(ledger, aggregateId))` (:28-35); the command is already registered with capability ADMIN and payload allow-list ["slice"] (daemon-command-registry.ts:53, :113). A ReviewerCalibration is three scalars and fits a slice with no shape change. So the authenticated durable WRITE path already exists and this task ships the READER plus a well-known ref constant -- a genuinely small task. REJECTED: (a) a dedicated command kind -- the runtime vocabulary is frozen with a full-coverage ratchet, so a new kind drags a much larger change for no capability the slice mechanism lacks; (b) a dedicated aggregate/event type -- same objection plus an upcaster; (c) reading calibration from a node spec file on disk -- any agent in the shared tree can write those, so it is not durable authority; (d) defaulting an absent calibration to {corpusRevision:"", sentinelPassed:false, staleness:"UNKNOWN"} -- see the risks; this is the single most likely wrong turn and it is forbidden. NOTE ON THE FILED TITLE: it says "record AND its installing command", and the create_task tool warned it might be two tasks. Measurement collapses it to one: the installing command already exists, so there is only the record and its reader to build.

CONSUMPTION: `calibrationCodes` (packages/review/src/reviewer-eligibility.ts:116-126) maps staleness STALE to REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_STALE, and staleness UNKNOWN or a failed sentinel or an empty corpusRevision to REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_UNPROVEN; `qualifyReviewerForAcceptance` (:135) is the ELIGIBILITY gate consulted before any proof or policy layer. It is a required field of VerifierAuthorityFacts (apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:16) and of the stored VerifierReceiptV1 (:42). PRODUCERS ON DISK: exactly one, the test fixture apps/daemon/src/review/review-test-fixtures.ts:249. review-acceptance.ts:116 only reads one back OUT of an already-recorded receipt, so it cannot be the source. The bootstrap ledger helpers this task composes are aggregateIdFor, commitAccepted, payloadObject, payloadRef, refuse, stateOf and versionOf, all exported from apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts. apps/daemon already declares @moe/review and @moe/store with apps/daemon importers in pnpm-lock.yaml, so no manifest edit is needed. A new .ts module in this repo needs a one-line .js bridge or it is invisible to the .js import graph.
planningNotes.risks: THE LOAD-BEARING RISK is a synthesised absent value. `{corpusRevision: "", sentinelPassed: false, staleness: "UNKNOWN"}` is a perfectly legal ReviewerCalibration that reviewer-eligibility maps to REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_UNPROVEN -- so returning it when nothing is installed LOOKS fail-closed and passes a careless review, while actually fabricating a durable fact: it asserts a calibration exists and is unproven, when the truth is none exists. Epic rail 4 requires missing evidence to stay UNKNOWN without gaining authority, and the contract's own comment says UNKNOWN is "unproven, never probably fine". Only a test asserting the REFUSAL code catches this, which is why drill 2 targets it specifically. Second, validate staleness against the imported public REVIEW_CALIBRATION_STALENESS rather than a local copy -- a restated set detaches silently the day the frozen set changes, and the test would still pass. Third, "nothing installed" and "installed but unreadable" are different facts needing distinct codes; collapsing them makes a later guard change invisible. Fourth, two layers can refuse here -- installPolicy's generic DAEMON_INGRESS BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID for a missing sliceRef, and this reader for malformed contents -- so every refusal test must assert WHICH layer answered, not merely that a refusal happened. Fifth, installPolicy's fold is last-write-wins per ref, so supersession is a real behaviour to test rather than assume. Sixth, a calibration slice becomes visible to validatePolicy as an installed ref; examine and state whether that matters rather than leaving it unexamined. Seventh, close every SqliteEventStore handle on every path -- a held handle kills the vitest worker. Finally, the consumer task-4dd4424c is BLOCKED, so DoD 6 is satisfied by naming its id and the intended call site, not by claiming a live edge exists.
